posts.cooked:
There is a question over a BGG that we would like some additional clarification on:

Quote from BGG poster MrFettucine :

So I had not used Mr. Fixer or Parse too much but I got them in a game and they seem to be a very potent combo. With Parse's Critical Multiplier, she can increase his damage by however many card's she discards. My friend had that out twice and discarded 3 cards (from one of her one shots), triggering his next attack to be +6. I had Jack Handle out with Mr. Fixer. And so if I read it correctly, he would hit all non-hero targets with 7 damage on his Strike power.

From my understanding, this is different from other area attacks from other heroes because only the first hit to a target would be +6 and the rest would be normal. But since Jack Handle says whenever he would deal damage to a target, he deals that much to all non-hero targets resulting in 7 damage to everyone except for heroes. It looks like Dual Crowbars would cause that damage increase to both targets hit as well.

I think I am looking at it correctly and if so, Parse and Mr. Fixer are a match made in heaven.

http://boardgamegeek.com/article/16889206#16889206

The question has basically come down to the disconnect between "next damage" and "nothing is SotM is simultaneous"

 

Also, another bit that came up is how much damage would Fixer deal if he targeted himself with his Strike power with Bloody Knuckles and Jack Handle in play. Since he would deal himself 5 damage is that 5 damage to all non-hero targets?

I've actually asked Christopher about Jack Handle in person. How Jack Handle is intended to work is you read Strike (or really anytime he deals damage) as Mr. Fixer deals all non-hero targets 1 melee damage. So Fixer would deal 7 damage to the first target and 1 to the rest.

Here's a link to where I posted a few rules questions, the first being the relevant one.

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
I'd have played it like the OP did - Parse discards cards until Fixer has +6 on his next attack, then Fixer does Strike, which does 7 damage, and Jack Handle, which says "whenever Mr. Fixer would deal damage to a target, he deals that much damage to all non-hero targets" makes it so that all non-hero targets take 7 damage.  Seems pretty straight forward to me.

The +6 damage was to his Strike, which was his "next time he deals damage", so that's taken care of.  Then Jack Handle takes that 7 damage, which is the "whenever Mr. Fixer would deal damage to a target", and applies it to all non-hero targets.  The damage isn't being modified anymore after the initial Strike, so there's no more "the first time" to worry about.  It's 7 (minus any DR the targets have, of course).

If Jack Handles said "whenever Mr. Fixer would use a power to deal damage to a target, he uses that power to damage all non-hero targets", I'd see everyone's point and say that the 7 damage was for the first hit but the others were normal unmodified Strikes.  But it says you take the damage you would have dealt (7) and deal that to all non-hero targets.

Here's what I have in my FAQ about this:

lastly, what exactly does “that much damage” mean? it means that whatever amount of damage was dealt after taking into account all modifiers is what is dealt to all non-hero cards, with no further modification. so, If mr. Fixer would deal 1 damage plus 2 due to modifiers, 3 damage is how much is done to all non-hero targets, not the 3 plus another 2. 

Further, it says

it means that instead of dealing the original damage, he deals that same amount and type of damage to all non-hero targets. effectively, the original damage mr. fixer would have dealt gets prevented and is replaced by the damage to all non-hero targets. 

Which makes it very clear that it's not the first damage is buffed but the others are not.  The first damage is prevented and is replaced by that same amount of damage to all non-hero targets. Unless that's now wrong somehow, that seems to cover it.
